quests.sentence: The policy that had been introduced when the government lost power was quietly abandoned by its successors
quests.correctAnswer: The policy that had been introduced when the government lost power was quietly abandoned by its successors.
quests.hint: Both 'that' clauses identify which policy and which government - are any of them non-restrictive?
quests.explanation: 'That had been introduced when the government lost power' identifies which specific policy. 'When the government lost power' identifies which government moment. Both clauses are restrictive and take no commas.

quests.sentence: The evidence pointed to only one conclusion the entire dataset had been deliberately altered
quests.correctAnswer: The evidence pointed to only one conclusion: the entire dataset had been deliberately altered.
quests.hint: 'Only one conclusion' announces that a specific revelation follows - what mark introduces it?
quests.explanation: A colon after 'only one conclusion' formally introduces the revelation. It is preferred over an em dash here because 'only one conclusion' sets up an expected announcement rather than a dramatic surprise.

quests.sentence: The drug which the regulator approved last year has shown promising results but the drug which was rejected at the same time has since been vindicated by new evidence
quests.correctAnswer: The drug that the regulator approved last year has shown promising results, but the drug that was rejected at the same time has since been vindicated by new evidence.
quests.hint: Both 'which' clauses identify which drug - they should use 'that' and take no commas. Two independent clauses join by 'but.'
quests.explanation: Restrictive clauses identifying specific nouns use 'that,' not 'which,' and take no commas. 'But' joining two independent clauses takes a comma before it.

quests.sentence: The intervention group n equals 47 and the control group n equals 45 did not differ significantly on any baseline measure
quests.correctAnswer: The intervention group (n = 47) and the control group (n = 45) did not differ significantly on any baseline measure.
quests.hint: Sample sizes are conventional parenthetical additions in scientific writing.
quests.explanation: Sample sizes (n = X) are enclosed in parentheses immediately after the group they describe. They are part of the noun phrase, not a separate clause.

quests.sentence: She had one choice and one choice only forgive him or lose him forever
quests.correctAnswer: She had one choice and one choice only-forgive him or lose him forever.
quests.hint: 'And one choice only' builds to a climax; the em dash releases the tension.
quests.explanation: An em dash introduces a dramatic revelation or list that completes an emphatic build-up. 'Forgive him or lose him forever' is the content of 'one choice only' and follows the em dash.

quests.sentence: He spent forty years building his career and then lost it all in a single day his reputation in ruins and his closest allies silent
quests.correctAnswer: He spent forty years building his career and then lost it all in a single day-his reputation in ruins and his closest allies silent.
quests.hint: The absolute phrase at the end dramatically describes the state of things - an em dash sets it off.
quests.explanation: An em dash before a closing absolute phrase ('his reputation in ruins…') adds dramatic weight. Commas would be too gentle for the gravity of what follows.

quests.sentence: The analysis examined demographic factors such as age sex and ethnicity health behaviours including diet exercise and smoking status and socioeconomic indicators comprising income education and employment
quests.correctAnswer: The analysis examined demographic factors such as age, sex, and ethnicity; health behaviours including diet, exercise, and smoking status; and socioeconomic indicators comprising income, education, and employment.
quests.hint: Three main categories each containing an internal serial list - semicolons between the three categories.
quests.explanation: When list items already contain commas (for their own sub-lists), semicolons separate the main items. Serial commas within each category remain.

quests.sentence: The task force identified four priority areas the healthcare system which had faced significant strain housing which remained unaffordable for many families education particularly early years provision and digital infrastructure especially in rural communities
quests.correctAnswer: The task force identified four priority areas: the healthcare system, which had faced significant strain; housing, which remained unaffordable for many families; education, particularly early years provision; and digital infrastructure, especially in rural communities.
quests.hint: Colon after 'four priority areas'; each item has an internal clause or qualifier - semicolons between the four items.
quests.explanation: A colon introduces the list. Each item's internal 'which' or 'particularly' clause creates internal commas, so semicolons separate the four main items.

quests.sentence: The committee found that the organisation had failed to conduct adequate background checks that it had not maintained appropriate records of complaints that it had systematically underpaid staff in breach of national minimum wage legislation and that it had made multiple false statements in its annual reports
quests.correctAnswer: The committee found that the organisation had failed to conduct adequate background checks, that it had not maintained appropriate records of complaints, that it had systematically underpaid staff in breach of national minimum wage legislation, and that it had made multiple false statements in its annual reports.
quests.hint: Four parallel 'that' clauses all depend on 'found' - serial commas separate them.
quests.explanation: Four parallel 'that' clauses as objects of 'found' use serial commas between them. Repeating 'that' before each clause maintains formal parallelism.

quests.sentence: It was too late she realised to change her mind now and perhaps it had always been too late even from the very beginning
quests.correctAnswer: It was too late, she realised, to change her mind now-and perhaps it had always been too late, even from the very beginning.
quests.hint: 'She realised' is a parenthetical attribution; the second clause is a sudden, deeper realisation - em dash before it.
quests.explanation: 'She realised' is a parenthetical free indirect discourse marker and takes commas. An em dash before the second clause 'and perhaps it had always been too late' marks the sudden, darker deepening of the thought.

quests.sentence: What was the point of it all he wondered staring at the ceiling there had to be something more than this surely some purpose he had simply failed to find
quests.correctAnswer: What was the point of it all, he wondered, staring at the ceiling; there had to be something more than this-surely some purpose he had simply failed to find.
quests.hint: Parenthetical 'he wondered'; participial phrase after; semicolon for the new thought; em dash before the hopeful qualification.
quests.explanation: 'He wondered' is a parenthetical attribution with commas. 'Staring at the ceiling' is a closing participial phrase. A semicolon links the new independent thought. An em dash before 'surely' introduces the tentative hope as a sudden, separate element.

quests.sentence: So it comes down to this she said quietly folding her hands in her lap either we trust each other completely or we have nothing worth saving
quests.correctAnswer: "So it comes down to this," she said quietly, folding her hands in her lap. "Either we trust each other completely, or we have nothing worth saving."
quests.hint: The attribution and action beat close the first sentence; the second sentence of dialogue starts fresh.
quests.explanation: The attribution 'she said quietly' and the participial phrase 'folding her hands' end the first sentence of dialogue. The second sentence is her full statement - a new set of quotation marks opens it, and 'or' joining two independent clauses takes a comma.

quests.sentence: In the event that the Supplier fails to deliver the Goods within the period specified in Schedule 1 as extended by any agreed variation and the Purchaser suffers loss as a direct result the Purchaser shall be entitled to recover such reasonable costs as it has incurred provided always that the Purchaser has taken all reasonable steps to mitigate its loss
quests.correctAnswer: In the event that the Supplier fails to deliver the Goods within the period specified in Schedule 1, as extended by any agreed variation, and the Purchaser suffers loss as a direct result, the Purchaser shall be entitled to recover such reasonable costs as it has incurred, provided always that the Purchaser has taken all reasonable steps to mitigate its loss.
quests.hint: Parenthetical 'as extended by any agreed variation'; end of the compound 'if' clause; 'provided always that' qualifies the remedy.
quests.explanation: 'As extended by any agreed variation' is a parenthetical and takes commas. The compound conditional clause ('if the Supplier fails…and the Purchaser suffers') ends with a comma before the main clause. 'Provided always that' qualifies the entitlement and takes a preceding comma.

quests.sentence: A material breach for the purposes of this Agreement means any breach that deprives the innocent party of substantially the whole of the benefit which it was intended by the parties should obtain from the performance of this Agreement
quests.correctAnswer: A 'material breach,' for the purposes of this Agreement, means any breach that deprives the innocent party of substantially the whole of the benefit which it was intended by the parties should obtain from the performance of this Agreement.
quests.hint: The defined term is in single quotes; 'for the purposes of this Agreement' is a parenthetical.
quests.explanation: Defined terms in contracts are enclosed in quotation marks and followed by a comma. 'For the purposes of this Agreement' is a parenthetical scoping phrase and is enclosed in commas.

quests.sentence: The Licensor warrants that to the best of its knowledge and belief as at the date of this Agreement the Software does not infringe any intellectual property rights of any third party in the jurisdictions in which the Licensee operates
quests.correctAnswer: The Licensor warrants that, to the best of its knowledge and belief as at the date of this Agreement, the Software does not infringe any intellectual property rights of any third party in the jurisdictions in which the Licensee operates.
quests.hint: 'To the best of its knowledge…' is a parenthetical qualification inserted inside the 'that' clause.
quests.explanation: The phrase 'to the best of its knowledge and belief as at the date of this Agreement' qualifies the scope of the warranty. Inserted inside the 'that' clause, it is enclosed in commas.

quests.sentence: The government insists the economy is recovering while the evidence suggests otherwise
quests.correctAnswer: The government insists the economy is recovering, while the evidence suggests otherwise.
quests.hint: 'While' here means 'whereas' - it introduces a contrast, not a simultaneous action.
quests.explanation: When 'while' means 'whereas' (introducing a contrast), a comma is appropriate before it. This distinguishes it from 'while' meaning 'during the time that' (simultaneity), which often needs no comma.

quests.sentence: She wore a pale, blue, silk evening gown to the awards ceremony.
quests.correctAnswer: She wore a pale blue silk evening gown to the awards ceremony.
quests.hint: Can you say 'pale and blue and silk evening gown' naturally? If not, these are cumulative adjectives.
quests.explanation: 'Pale,' 'blue,' and 'silk' are cumulative adjectives - each modifies the noun combination that follows it ('pale blue silk evening gown'). They cannot be reversed or joined with 'and' naturally, so no commas are used.

quests.sentence: She left early, so that she could meet her daughter from school.
quests.correctAnswer: She left early so that she could meet her daughter from school.
quests.hint: Does 'so that' showing purpose take a comma before it?
quests.explanation: 'So that' expressing purpose does not take a comma before it. The comma is only used before 'so' when it functions as a coordinating conjunction (meaning 'therefore'). 'So that' (= in order that) is a subordinating conjunction requiring no comma.

quests.sentence: The report described the current situation as deeply troubling and called for immediate action
quests.correctAnswer: The report described the current situation as 'deeply troubling' and called for 'immediate action.'
quests.hint: These are exact phrases from the report - mark them as quoted material.
quests.explanation: Exact phrases taken from a source and used within a sentence are enclosed in single quotation marks (British style). The final period falls inside the closing quotation mark when it closes the sentence.

quests.sentence: The transition to renewable energy argues Taylor is not merely an economic necessity but an existential imperative
quests.correctAnswer: "The transition to renewable energy," argues Taylor, "is not merely an economic necessity but an existential imperative."
quests.hint: 'Argues Taylor' interrupts the quoted sentence - a split quotation with the attribution mid-quote.
quests.explanation: A split quotation has its attribution ('argues Taylor') between two halves. A comma ends the first half inside the closing mark; a comma follows the attribution before the second half opens.

quests.sentence: Smith 2023 contends that the failure to account for intersectionality in early studies significantly skewed the results and concludes that the field requires a fundamental methodological reorientation
quests.correctAnswer: Smith (2023) contends that 'the failure to account for intersectionality in early studies significantly skewed the results' and concludes that 'the field requires a fundamental methodological reorientation.'
quests.hint: The year goes in parentheses; the two quoted clauses are the author's exact words.
quests.explanation: In-text citations place the year in parentheses after the author's name. The author's exact words, when integrated into a sentence, are enclosed in single quotation marks (British style). The period falls inside the final closing quote mark when it ends the sentence.

quests.sentence: Participants were included if they met the following criteria were aged between 18 and 65 had a confirmed diagnosis of type 2 diabetes had no comorbid psychiatric conditions and had not received any pharmacological treatment in the preceding three months
quests.correctAnswer: Participants were included if they met the following criteria: were aged between 18 and 65, had a confirmed diagnosis of type 2 diabetes, had no comorbid psychiatric conditions, and had not received any pharmacological treatment in the preceding three months.
quests.hint: 'The following criteria' signals a list (colon); four parallel conditions use serial commas.
quests.explanation: 'The following criteria' announces a list and requires a colon. The four parallel conditions form a serial list separated by commas.

quests.sentence: Taken together the results which are broadly consistent with the findings of Williams et al 2022 suggest that the effect size is smaller than previously estimated and that additional moderating variables may need to be considered in future research
quests.correctAnswer: Taken together, the results, which are broadly consistent with the findings of Williams et al. (2022), suggest that the effect size is smaller than previously estimated and that additional moderating variables may need to be considered in future research.
quests.hint: Opening participial; non-restrictive 'which' clause with citation; two parallel 'that' clauses (no comma before 'and that').
quests.explanation: 'Taken together' is an opening participial phrase taking a comma. The 'which' clause is non-restrictive and takes commas. 'Et al.' takes a period. The year goes in parentheses. The two parallel 'that' clauses both depend on 'suggest' - no comma before 'and that.'

quests.sentence: The analysis of variance revealed a significant interaction effect F 2 147 equals 8.34 p less than .001 partial eta squared equals .10 indicating that the effect of the intervention varied as a function of age group
quests.correctAnswer: The analysis of variance revealed a significant interaction effect (F(2, 147) = 8.34, p < .001, partial η² = .10), indicating that the effect of the intervention varied as a function of age group.
quests.hint: Statistical values go in parentheses; commas separate the statistics within; closing participial phrase after.
quests.explanation: The F-statistic with its degrees of freedom and associated p-value and effect size are all enclosed in parentheses. Commas separate the statistical values within the parentheses. The closing participial phrase ('indicating that…') takes a preceding comma.

quests.sentence: In a society where the pace of technological change is accelerating exponentially and where the skills that were valuable a decade ago may be obsolete within five years the ability to learn adapt and apply knowledge in novel contexts has become if anything more important than the mere possession of qualifications
quests.correctAnswer: In a society where the pace of technological change is accelerating exponentially and where the skills that were valuable a decade ago may be obsolete within five years, the ability to learn, adapt, and apply knowledge in novel contexts has become, if anything, more important than the mere possession of qualifications.
quests.hint: Long 'where' clause (with restrictive 'that' inside); serial comma list of three verbs; 'if anything' parenthetical.
quests.explanation: The long introductory 'where' clause ends with a comma. The three parallel verbs ('learn, adapt, and apply') use serial commas. 'If anything' is a parenthetical concessive and takes commas.

quests.sentence: While it would be premature to draw firm causal conclusions from a single cross-sectional study the consistency of the findings across multiple subgroups and their alignment with the predictions of the theoretical model provides at least tentative support for the proposed mechanism
quests.correctAnswer: While it would be premature to draw firm causal conclusions from a single cross-sectional study, the consistency of the findings across multiple subgroups and their alignment with the predictions of the theoretical model provides at least tentative support for the proposed mechanism.
quests.hint: 'While' clause takes a comma; no comma inside the 'and' joining two noun phrases as the compound subject.
quests.explanation: The introductory 'while' clause takes a comma before the main clause. 'The consistency…and their alignment' form a compound subject joined by 'and' - no comma is needed between the two noun phrases.

quests.sentence: What appears at first glance to be a straightforward methodological question turns out on closer examination to involve a series of deeply contested assumptions about the nature of causation the limits of quantitative inference and the relationship between statistical significance and practical importance
quests.correctAnswer: What appears at first glance to be a straightforward methodological question turns out, on closer examination, to involve a series of deeply contested assumptions about the nature of causation, the limits of quantitative inference, and the relationship between statistical significance and practical importance.
quests.hint: 'On closer examination' is a parenthetical adverb phrase mid-clause; three-item list after 'about.'
quests.explanation: 'On closer examination' inserted into the main clause is parenthetical and takes commas. The three parallel noun phrases after 'about' form a serial list with commas.

quests.sentence: Having studied the proposals at length the committee a body established under section 14 of the Act reached the conclusion that the plans while ambitious were not it believed practically deliverable within the proposed timeframe
quests.correctAnswer: Having studied the proposals at length, the committee, a body established under section 14 of the Act, reached the conclusion that the plans, while ambitious, were not, it believed, practically deliverable within the proposed timeframe.
quests.hint: Participial opener; appositive; parenthetical 'while ambitious'; parenthetical 'it believed' - four punctuation tasks.
quests.explanation: The participial opener takes a comma. The appositive takes commas. 'While ambitious' is a concessive parenthetical and takes commas. 'It believed' is a parenthetical attribution and takes commas.

quests.sentence: The chancellor whose announcement yesterday caught the markets off guard and whose subsequent clarification did little to restore confidence will face questions in parliament this afternoon a session that many expect to be particularly bruising
quests.correctAnswer: The chancellor, whose announcement yesterday caught the markets off guard and whose subsequent clarification did little to restore confidence, will face questions in parliament this afternoon-a session that many expect to be particularly bruising.
quests.hint: One 'whose' clause with two parts (commas); em dash before the dramatic appositive at the end.
quests.explanation: The non-restrictive 'whose' clause with two conjoined parts takes one pair of commas. An em dash before 'a session…' introduces the dramatic elaborating appositive.

quests.sentence: The history of science is littered with examples of theories that were once considered beyond question subsequently being overturned by new evidence a process that Thomas Kuhn famously described as a paradigm shift and that reminds us that scientific knowledge is always provisional always revisable and always in some sense incomplete
quests.correctAnswer: The history of science is littered with examples of theories that were once considered beyond question subsequently being overturned by new evidence-a process that Thomas Kuhn famously described as a 'paradigm shift' and that reminds us that scientific knowledge is always provisional, always revisable, and always in some sense incomplete.
quests.hint: Em dash before the dramatic appositive; coined term in single quotes; serial 'always' clauses with commas.
quests.explanation: An em dash introduces the dramatic appositive 'a process…' The coined technical term 'paradigm shift' is in single quotes. The three parallel 'always' clauses ('always provisional, always revisable, and always in some sense incomplete') use serial commas.
